findings.description: `Principal.instanceFrom` sets businessId to `user.getId()` (Principal.java:181), and a self-registered player's profile is a separate row whose `user_id` points to that account (PlayerProfile.userId). `currentPlayerProfileId()` still returns `requireCurrentUserId()` and calls `playerProfileRepository.findById(userId)`, so the upload lookup finds no profile and returns 403. `/my` and `/quotas/me` use the user id as ownerId, but uploads (and VideoAccessGuard's parent-link check) key on the profile id, so the list and quota are always empty or wrong. The comments saying "businessId = PlayerProfile.id" contradict how the Principal is actually built.
findings.title: Player video endpoints use the account's user id as if it were the PlayerProfile id, so self-registered players can't upload or see their own videos
findings.verification: Confirmed from Principal.instanceFrom and ShadowAccountService.createSelfOwnedPlayerProfile, which stores userId on a new profile with its own TSID. It would only work if a user id happened to equal some profile id, and in that case the upload would be written to a stranger's profile.

findings.description: PlayerRegistrationService gives new players only the `ROLE_PLAYER` authority. `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('ROLE_USER')")` on `/player/uploads/initiate`, and `hasAnyRole('ROLE_USER','ROLE_COACH')` on `/my` and `/quotas/me`, therefore return 403 for every real player. Generic ROLE_USER accounts that have no player profile are the only ones let in, so the HOMEWORK upload flow is unreachable for its intended users.
findings.title: Player upload endpoint requires ROLE_USER, but self-registered players only get ROLE_PLAYER
findings.verification: Check whether ROLE_PLAYER users are also given ROLE_USER anywhere else (for example a role hierarchy bean). PlayerRegistrationService:96 assigns only ROLE_PLAYER.

findings.description: For coach videos, ownerId is the coach profile UUID, but the fallback compares it to `securityUtil.getCurrentUserName()`, which returns the email (VideoAccessGuard's own javadoc says this never matches). So a coach calling `/api/video/{id}/events` or `/status` on their own DRILL_DEMO/COACH_REVIEW upload always gets MISSING_RIGHTS, and the upload-progress UI can't track processing. For player videos, it compares businessId (user id) with ownerId (profile id), so self-registered players are denied too, and parents/admins allowed by VideoAccessGuard are never allowed here.
findings.title: Video event/status ownership check compares a coach video's profile UUID with the caller's username (email), so coaches are always denied
findings.verification: Upload a video as a coach and call GET /api/video/{id}/status. It returns 403.

findings.description: `isOwner` compares the caller's businessId (user id) with a player video's ownerId, which is `PlayerProfile.id` (written as `String.valueOf(profile.getId())` in VideoResource). For a self-registered adult player these ids are different, and there is no ParentPlayerLink, so `canPlay` and `canDelete` throw PlaybackDenied/DeletionNotAuthorised when the player tries to play or delete their own HOMEWORK video. The owner check needs to resolve the profile through `findByUserId`, the way PlayerOwnershipGuard does.
findings.title: VideoAccessGuard owner check never matches a self-registered player's own video
findings.verification: Confirm that ownerId values for HOMEWORK videos in the `video` table are player_profiles.id values, not user ids.

findings.description: `getMyPlayerSubscription` now uses `playerOwnershipGuard`, which accepts self-owned profiles, and `SubscriptionService.assertPlayerOwnership` also accepts `existsByIdAndUserId`. But the three mutating endpoints are still gated by `HAS_PARENT_ROLE`, which a ROLE_PLAYER account doesn't have. An adult player who opens their subscription page and clicks subscribe, upgrade or cancel gets 403, so they can't stop a paid subscription themselves. These endpoints contradict the skillars-deferred-147 intent and the service's own ownership rules.
findings.title: Self-registered players can view their own subscription but can't subscribe, change tier or cancel
findings.verification: Log in as a self-registered ROLE_PLAYER and call DELETE /api/payment/subscriptions/player?playerId=<own>. It returns 403.

findings.description: The GET endpoint uses `playerOwnershipGuard`, which now admits self-owned players. `POST /homework/{id}/complete` requires `HAS_PARENT_ROLE`, and the service checks ownership with `findByIdAndParentId(playerId, callerId)`, which is always empty when `parent_id` is null. An adult player sees their Locker Room drills but gets 403 (or a 404 'Assignment not found' if they had the role) when completing them, so completion status never updates for them.
findings.title: Homework completion is parent-only, so a self-registered player can list homework but never mark it complete

findings.description: Two simultaneous completes (for example a double-click) both pass `existsByAssignmentId`. The loser's `saveAndFlush` throws DataIntegrityViolationException from the repository proxy, whose transactional interceptor marks the shared outer transaction rollback-only before the catch swallows it. When `markComplete`'s @Transactional tries to commit, it throws UnexpectedRollbackException, so the client gets a 500 despite the 'idempotent, ignore' comment. The failed flush also leaves the Hibernate session in an undefined state.
findings.title: Concurrent duplicate markComplete returns 500 instead of the intended idempotent 200
findings.verification: Integration-test two parallel markComplete calls on the same assignment and check the second response status.

findings.description: Only DataIntegrityViolationException is caught per drill. If `erasureGuard.isErasedUnderLock` hits NOWAIT lock contention (PessimisticLockingFailureException) or any transient DB error on drill 1, the exception escapes the loop. The @Async handler drops it after the finally block, so drill 2 is never assigned. A replayed event is the only way to recover, and nothing triggers one.
findings.title: An exception other than duplicate-key in a per-drill transaction aborts the remaining homework drills with no retry
findings.verification: Check whether isErasedUnderLock uses findByIdForUpdate (NOWAIT) without its own retry, and whether any DLQ or retry wraps this @Async listener.
